instruction: Add one tab of indent to every line in test.py.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey("ctrl", "s"); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully selected lines 2-10 in VS Code and pressed Tab to indent them by one level, then saved the file. Completed in 7 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can select line ranges in VS Code (click + shift-click), press Tab to indent, save files with Ctrl+S, dismiss notifications
metadata.task_rationale: Tests selecting all lines (including line 1) and indenting, requiring Ctrl+A or click on line 1 + shift-click on line 10
metadata.explanation: Task requires selecting all 10 lines and pressing Tab to add one level of indentation to every line. Getter reads the file and returns all lines. Metric checks all 10 lines match expected indented content. Partial credit: 0.1 per correct line.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads the file from the VM filesystem and returns all lines as a list, which is the right state to extract for this task.
Metric correctly accesses expected.get('expected_lines') — compatible with the framework's get_rule behavior where expected IS the rules dict.
All 10 lines are verified with exact string matching and partial credit (0.1 per line), providing complete coverage of the instruction.
Postconfig correctly saves the file (Ctrl+S) before the getter reads it, ensuring fresh state.
Expected values correctly show each original line with 4 additional leading spaces (one VS Code tab), consistent with VS Code's default insertSpaces=true and tabSize=4 settings.

Minor concern: exact string matching assumes VS Code uses spaces for Tab (the default). If the VM's VS Code were configured to insert literal tab characters, verification would fail. This is unlikely with default settings but worth noting.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider making the comparison slightly more flexible to handle both tab characters and spaces (e.g., normalize tabs to spaces before comparison), though this is a minor concern given VS Code defaults.
